summary:
North Rhine-Westphalia stands under the German federal framework. The Self-Determination Act, in force since 1 November 2024, sets the default rule for housing a detained trans visitor: under § 6(1) the person's legal gender entry governs placement unless state law provides otherwise. Prison administration is dealt with at Land level, and the sources reviewed carry no trans-specific placement statute for North Rhine-Westphalia, so the federal default is the operative standard here rather than a local carve-out.

The Verfassungsblog analysis of 18 March 2026 examines how the Länder apply that provision. Several states' exception clauses are criticised for singling out trans inmates specifically, while abstract clauses of the kind adopted in Rhineland-Palatinate are defended as compliant. North Rhine-Westphalia has enacted neither form, which leaves a trans visitor sentenced in the Land to be housed on the basis of registered gender unless an individual authority decides otherwise.

Placement outcomes under that default have not been uniform, and the federal Act itself is under political pressure: a Bundesrat initiative to tighten it was put forward by other states in July 2026. Any tightening would bind North Rhine-Westphalia as it binds every other Land.

North Rhine-Westphalia holds its own evidence base on trans residents. On 25 April 2025 the Land government published the study „Queer durch NRW – Lebenslagen und Erfahrungen von LSBTIQ*“, the first comprehensive dataset on the living situations of lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans*, inter*, queer and non-binary people in the Land. It combined quantitative online surveys of more than 5,000 LSBTIQ* respondents, 775 relatives and over 5,000 professionals with qualitative focus groups and expert interviews.

The study covers discrimination, violence and safety; health, care and ageing; and integration, migration and flight. It was commissioned under Landtag resolution Drucksache 18/6360 to give the state's „Aktionsplan für Vielfalt und gegen Homo- und Transfeindlichkeit“ a broader data basis.

The Land has enacted no trans-specific statute, and its anti-homo- and transphobia action plan now rests on this dataset rather than on legislation.
tangentialFactors:
The federal placement rule is contested at Bundesrat level. An initiative to tighten the Self-Determination Act followed the July 2026 reporting on a trans prisoner held in a men's prison despite a completed legal gender change; the sponsoring states were Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia, not North Rhine-Westphalia. A tightening would raise the bar for a visitor who relies on registered gender for housing in the Land.

North Rhine-Westphalia's silence on trans prison placement cuts both ways. It means no statute names trans inmates as a separate category, which is the drafting criticised in the Verfassungsblog analysis, but it also means no abstract clause of the Rhineland-Palatinate kind has been written to give prison administrations a settled procedure.

The Land's own study is a comparatively substantial official undertaking for a sub-national unit, with survey samples on the scale of several thousand respondents in a single Land, and it is the reference point for state policy on hostility toward trans people.
localsOnly:
North Rhine-Westphalia's anti-discrimination and diversity policy is driven from the Land ministry, which maintains an LSBTIQ* section and commissioned the „Queer durch NRW“ study under Landtag resolution Drucksache 18/6360. The „Aktionsplan für Vielfalt und gegen Homo- und Transfeindlichkeit“ is the operative policy instrument for residents, and its evidentiary base is the 2025 study rather than new legislation.

Residents held in the Land's prisons are housed under the federal default of § 6(1) of the Self-Determination Act, since no North Rhine-Westphalia correctional provision on trans placement is on file. The practical outcome therefore depends on the individual prison administration's reading of the registered gender entry.

The study's trans*-specific findings on discrimination, violence and safety, and on health, care and ageing, are held at Land level and inform resident-facing services; the sources reviewed do not itemise those findings.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether North Rhine-Westphalia prison administrations in practice follow registered gender entry, and how often placement is reviewed or reversed at intake, is unresolved: no Land-specific trans placement statute and no Land-specific placement case appear in the sources reviewed.

The trans*-specific results of the „Queer durch NRW“ study are not itemised in the sources reviewed, so the scale of discrimination or violence reported by trans residents in the Land cannot be stated here.

No incident of violence against a trans visitor in North Rhine-Westphalia, and no Land-level complaint or court ruling on facilities, documents or screening, is recorded in the sources reviewed.

The content of the Land's „Aktionsplan für Vielfalt und gegen Homo- und Transfeindlichkeit“ beyond its commissioning basis, and any enforcement record under it, is not sourced.
